items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: a Steely Dan meets Jaco meets Dave Matthews

ctx.x: going to work a lot more for sure. And all those things I mean I think — I always say when I give clinics it’s like you’re opening a flower shop and there’s already five or six flower shops within a couple mile radius of you. So that’s not to say that you can’t be successful, but what’s going to make you more successful? So you know, oh that person always opens at 8:15 but it says 8:00 and, you know I hate going there because their person is always late and I need to get in and out of there so I can go to work or…

Well said. I want to talk about compositional inspiration for a moment. I was looking at your catalogue and I’m assuming these are your tunes or maybe your son’s. There was this song called “A Life Lived” from 9/11 time, and then on the other spectrum there’s something called “Stomper” which you described as a Steely Dan meets Jaco meets Dave Matthews.
That’s very generous of me to describe that that way.
